target_customer: Leisure travelers seeking discounted airfare and hotels, later corporate travel managers and travel agencies
problem: Travelers want deep discounts, and airlines want to sell distressed inventory without damaging their brand.
business_model: Consumer booking commissions, then B2B travel technology licensing

competitors.name: Priceline
competitors.what: Opaque name your own price and Express Deals for air and hotels

competitors.name: Hotwire
competitors.what: Opaque discounted airfare, hotels and cars

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed airline and hotel inventory integrations and a pricing model that worked for both consumers and airlines, per TechCrunch.

defensibility.rationale: Priceline and Hotwire already ran opaque models, and the differentiator was a surprise destination, which is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; BCD Travel bought the technology assets in January 2016 after a 2014 pivot to corporate travel.

market_need_then: Opaque booking was an established category through Priceline and Hotwire, and airlines wanted channels for discounted seats; the YC blog in July 2013 reported about 5M USD raised.

brand_strength.rationale: No sourced brand coverage beyond product reviews; name is a plain phrase.

pivots.from: Consumer opaque airfare and hotel site
pivots.to: Cloud based corporate travel technology for agencies and travel management companies
pivots.why: PhocusWire reported the B2B pivot as profitable; consumer business exited

outcome_analysis: GetGoing raised a seed round and about 5M USD in total by July 2013, then pivoted in 2014 to B2B travel technology that PhocusWire called profitable. BCD Travel bought the technology assets in January 2016 and the CEO joined BCD, which Skift called a soft landing, so it was a small acquisition rather than a venture outcome.
notes: YC listing has no website. The 3M USD seed rests on a single database (startupintros); Seedtable lists 2.5M USD dated 2012-01, likely the same round. YC blog (2013-07-24) says about 5M USD raised in total, so rounds are missing; PhocusWire (unopened, 403) is reported by search to name investors Alexis Ohanian and Yuri Milner. CB Insights figures (20K USD) judged unreliable. Priceline and Hotwire entries rest on the PhocusWire article title; its date could not be read and the 2013-07 date is a guess bounded by the YC blog, so treat as approximate. Kayak source is nine months after the batch. Founder backgrounds not given by sources. Acquisition was an asset purchase. The YC directory marks the company Inactive because it was acquired; exit.type acquisition is correct and the conflict is only the directory label.
